key_insight: ORDERS shows that a norm-ranked, geometrically weighted aggregation rule can slightly improve personalized federated learning, but most gains are small and depend heavily on the evaluation endpoint.
engineering_relevance: For practical FL systems, the paper suggests server-side weighting and client-private adaptation can help, yet implementation complexity may outweigh modest accuracy and payload benefits.
method: Shared backbone plus client-specific residual adapter and classifier
Server aggregates same-round client updates using descending update-norm ranks with geometric weights
Includes feature alignment and private-parameter perturbation variants
evidence_signal: The study reports 80 runs across eight configurations, two datasets, and five seeds; ORDERS reaches 80.51% native accuracy on CIFAR-10 and 74.71% on Sent140.
watch_item: Reported improvements are narrow and endpoint-dependent, so gains may not generalize beyond the fixed partition, training protocol, and post-fine-tuning setup.
paper_title: ORDERS: An Empirical Study of Norm-Rank Aggregation for Personalized Federated Learning
